newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn surges near limit on fund buying, cattle.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn surges near limit on fund buying, cattle.

text.p: CBOT corn futures surged nearly their 12-cent-per-bushel limit by the close on huge fund buying coupled with bullish fuel from a government cattle report, traders said.
"There were some (news) items out but not enough to do this, I think it's overdone. The cattle on feed report was friendly but not enough to do this," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter Reynolds.
USDA Friday said the number of cattle placed on feed during January in the seven key feeding states in the U.S. was 25 percent above the placements during January a year ago.
Analysts were expecting the placmements figure to be nearer 7.5 percent above a year ago.
But the key to Tuesday's surge which drove nearby March corn through key resistance near the $2.80 level was the relentless buying by commodity funds, traders said.

"It was huge fund buying, somewhere between 80 million and 100 million bushels. Funds reversed position. They were short and are going long," said Paul Haugens, vice president for Chicago-based trade house FIMAT Futures.
Corn closed five to 10-1/4 cents per bushel higher, with March up 8-3/4 at $2.82-3/4.

The session high for March corn was $2.83 per bushel, the highest level since $2.82 was touched on October 25 and some traders said corn was headed for the $2.90 mark on key technical trading charts. A chart gap was set on October 25 because the session high that day equaled the session low the previous day. That gap was considered a key ceiling for the market to break through.
"It's headed to the $2.90 area but there was increased selling at the upper end of this range," said Mark Cermak of O'Connor and Co.
Nearby March corn gapped to a session high of $2.81 per bushel in early fast dealings.
"We took out the recent high ($2.77-1/4 set January 28) in March and we hit stops," a trader said. The buy stops triggered the fast markets and active fund buying, the traders said.
Traders said Friday's Commodity Futures Trading Commission Commitments of Traders report sent out bullish flags for the corn market.
"It was a surprisingly large short of 84 million to perhaps long after today. They had to have bought 80 to 100 million bushels of corn," a trader said.
"We've been in a trading range for over two months and this is our upside breakout," the trader noted.
CFTC said as of Tuesday, non-commercials, including funds, were short corn by roughly 215.7 million bushels and long by 131.4 million bushels.

Support also came from dry weather in South Africa which continued to stir ideas of potential corn exports to that region but the fund buying in corn captured most of the attention as did early commercial demand.
USDA's weekly export inspections total for the week ended February 13 totaled 32.347 million bushels, below trade expectations for 35 million to 41 million bushels.

Traders said Rosenthal Collins bought seven million bushels of March and 15 million May, Smith Barney bought nine million May, Griffin Trading bought eight million May and Cargill Investor Services bought eight million bushels of March and bought seven million bushels of July.

ADM Investor Services sold five million bushels of March as did Cargill Inc and Farmers Commodities Corp. Term Commodities sold four million July and Credit Agrico sold five million bushels of March, traders said.
Corn futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 100,000 contract, up sharply from the 68,415 contracts traded Friday.

In corn options, Credit Agrico sold 2,000 March $2.80 calls at 1-1/2 to two cents, Prudential Securities bought 2,000 March $2.80 calls at two to 2-1/4 cents and Smith Barney sold 2,500 March $2.80 calls at 1-1/2 to 2-1/2 cents.
Corn options volume was estimated at 22,000 contracts, above the 18,910 traded Friday.
